review_text: I’ve been wanting to try this product out ever since it became viral on social media. However, I wasn’t really intrigued by any of the scents until the peppermint one came out recently and decided I’d finally splurge on it! I’ve been using this product for a few weeks now and have used it most nights (enough to know how long it wears and ultimately, enough to review the product with honesty). First things first, I would not consider this an overnight lip mask as it only lasts about an hour/hour and a half (that’s even pushing it) after application. My routine with this is usually to apply it right before I head to bed. I’ll usually browse through my phone/read a book for an hour or so before I actually sleep. Throughout that hour or so, I am usually not talking or doing anything that would cause the product to disappear from my lips, but somehow, it still does not stay longer than the duration I mentioned above. Furthermore, I have not noticed a change in the moisture/hydration of my lips in the mornings after applying this the nights before. At times, I even find that my lips are drier after I use this product. The only components that I enjoy about this product is that it comes with a good amount and the peppermint scent is very refreshing. I find that this lip sleeping mask is only really benefiting me when I want to lather something on my lips to make it slippery and smooth for an hour (like lip balms that don’t have other uses but to make your lips feel smooth in that moment).I would not recommend this product and I will not be repurchasing it.

review_text: This review is for the new Pumpkin Spice “flavored“ lip mask.  Just wanted to show you guys the color and compare it to the Gingersnap one which was discontinued and which I’m still hoping they will bring back... So, the texture and feel on the lips are the same as all the other Laneige lip masks.  It feels smooth, not grainy at all, kind of like a thick gel but without being sticky or leaving any kind of residue on the lips as it fades.  Those are the positive attributes of this one BUT, sadly, as with the previous limited edition of the Cherry one, I’m disappointed with the scent.  It does smell vaguely of pumpkin spice but in a plasticky, fake kind of way and without any kind of sweetness added to it.  After a couple of minutes on the lips the smell dissipates completely and the slight aftertaste you are left with is reminiscent of vaseline in some way, very artificial...Compared to my beloved Gingersnap (on the left in the included picture), it doesn’t add even the slightest bit of tint to your lips and, of course, doesn’t smell nearly as good.  So, if you are looking to replace your Gingersnap mask (like me) this won’t do it but overall, it’s a good product and does the job it’s intended for.  Moisturizing, doesn’t interfere with other products you plan to apply afterward (when used during the day) and is definitely suitable for this time of the year (I’m writing this in September).  So, if you are just looking for something to “refresh“ your Laneige arsenal, this would be a good addition to it but don’t expect a sweet, gourmand pumpkin spice smell and/or taste.

I have to keep chapstick in many rooms in my house, as well as in my car and all of my purses, so that I don’t ever go without it on accident. However, I just really grew to love it and, slowly iver time, I began choosing this over my Burt’s Bee’s chapstick that had been my favorite and only kind I would use. Originally, I bought this mask in a kit, so it was a smaller container. The full size container is too big for me to carry around and I don’t want to contaminate it. So what I did was I kept the small container and cleaned it and then I added some from the big to the small. Any time I need to add more to the small container, I clean it/sanitize it beforehand and do my best to avoid contaminating the big container (especially since it’s going to lay me a really long time!).

review_text: I purchased this lip mask over the holidays as I’ve been struggling with dry lips this winter. I had read the reviews and it seemed very well liked overall! I’m glad I did, because after about two weeks of straight usage, my lips have gotten softer and less cracked. The initial dryness that it caused, however, was really quite startling. I really like the light, sweet scent the product has, and it feels very creamy on the lips. It gives a beautiful shine. It does, however, have a chemically sort of taste if you accidentally ingest it. When I wake up in the morning, I feel that the product has fully absorbed into my lips, and that they do feel softer. I saw some people say that they felt it reduced any fine lines or wrinkles they were developing on their lips, but that hasn’t really been the case for me. I’m not sure if it’s because I haven’t been using it long enough, or if it’s because my wrinkles are just starting to form, but I haven’t seen this benefit. Overall, I think it’s a pretty nice product, I think it takes some time and patience getting used to. I’m not sure if I’ll buy this again in be future, I may try one of the other ones just to give it a fair chance. I think the value of the product is good for how much money you pay vs. what you get in the container. I also think that the presentation of the product is quite cute.

review_text: The Good: I’ve been reaching for this stuff for 3-4 years straight which is truly impressive and speaks for itself. I have tried both the Berry and Vanilla versions (and finished several jars of each) and anytime a large sale rolls around I usually toss one into my cart. The product smell is an overall HUGE hit (except for the Gummy Bear scent that smells horrific to me and is their only true miss in the scent category). One of the top perks is just how yummy this smells on the lips, I reach for it often during times when my lips just need a little bit of a pick-me-up. This is a light-weight type of product, not what you’d expect out of something labeled a “mask“ but I do enjoy how glide-able it is on the lips in comparison to thicker masks/balms. The jar is extremely durable and its easy to tag it along inside a bag or even on airline travels. I also noticed over the years that I oftentimes bring this along on plane rides with me, it’s a godsend for that dry airplane air (if you know, you know). The Bad: As previously stated the Gummy Bear scent is something you should avoid if you actually like gummy bears because it smells way more like children’s cough syrup to me. Also, I have to say I would NOT consider this a mask. If you are looking for something to combat HARSH northern winters this simply won’t cut it most of the time and you need to purchase a different product. I would consider this more of a hydrating lip “cream“ as opposed to a mask and I really think that would be a more appropriate labeling for this product. The Ugly/Honest: This product lasts a long time which is great but the fact that you have to dig your finger into this to get product is a little off-putting. I know they used to come with a little tiny plastic scooper (maybe they still do) but it’s so tiny and flimsy that I always end up losing mine somewhere to no avail. Overall, this is a decent product but it’s NOT a lip mask.

review_text: This a a wall of text but I genuinely have to put this out there.I LOVED this product and purchased it religiously for several years. It was my favorite serum. But recently they have changed the formula, and now it is, for me, completely unusable. I’m going to preface this by saying that once I found a good skincare routine, I stuck with it. I never changed ANYTHING, I just bought more of what I’d been using when I ran low.With the old formula, I had absolutely zero irritation and my skin was breakout free. It didn’t feel overly-sensitive, and the texture was nice. When I ran out of my last tube of the old formula, I bought a new one and you could immediately tell it was different. The consistency was sticky and sort of greasy, the color was off, and the scent was almost rancid. It used to smell sort of like maple syrup, and it used to feel really pleasant to apply in terms of consistency and a nice, warming sensation. The old formula soaked in quickly and didn’t leave a weird film on my skin. The new formula gave me a stinging, burning sensation on application, never completely absorbed and left my skin feeling sticky. By morning (I applied it before bed), my skin was super greasy, which never happened before. It was also red and splotchy, and felt irritated.After about week of hoping maybe it was something else - like I said, I loved this serum before - I started having breakouts all over my face and neck, which I had also not had an issue with before. I also had a constant itchy, burning feeling on my neck. Stopped using it and switched to another retinol (which was unfortunately not the reasonable price point of INKey) and my skin went back to normal. It’s legitimately no longer a good product. I would not even say your mileage may vary - I would not feel comfortable recommending this to anyone.

review_text: I know the name says anti-aging but retinol was connected to acne initially so I decided to give it a shot as someone who has had hormonal acne for over 5 years. review_text: I’ve been using the Retinol Serum for awhile now, (this is my 3rd tube), and it does take a while to see results. Having said that, I do note that this is a more mild dosing of Retinol and there are others out there that are stronger, but your skin may take a “hit“ in that it might become reddened or peel or sting/burn when the product is applied; which is why I prefer this type of retinol serum. It works on one’s skin without the discomfort associated with many retinoids out there. I also appreciate the price point of the Inkey List’s products, as you can literally build an entire skin care routine from the ground up, and include two to three serums and/or treatment items as well. You can’t say that with many brands out there with the same types of products and get the same type of results. I am often asked “What do you use on your skin?“ I usually answer “Oh I use a few things from different lines.“ because I do, but it’s the products that perform that you tend to not reveal that much, as you want to keep those to yourself!This is one of those products, as it does work and you can recommend it to others knowing that it actually does something for your skin. At least for me, I can say “Yes“ I benefit from this particular serum. If you’re new to retinoids this would be a good one to start off with, as it is gentle, and you wouldn’t have to worry about adverse affects on your skin. But patch testing is always a good idea. Give it a try, It works for me!

review_text: So, I am definitely not new to retinol, as I have been getting prescription retinol for years. I have a very sensitive, combination skin type that is acne prone. I’ve been in the dermatigists office since I was 9. To give you an idea of my skincare routine the past 10 years, I use a benzoyl peroxide wash at least 3 times a week, about the same amount of lactic acid per week (sometimes I’ll use clarisonic instead), retinol, and topical clindamycin. Obviously, these products are all VERY drying without a good moisturizer. I really like this product though because I tend to peel a lot (ew!) from the prescription retinol recently (guess my skin type changed a little with age now that I’m 23) but this stuff is definitely more gentle than any one I’ve ever used.I have tried both drug store retinols and high end retinols. I wanted to try something different because I still hadnt found one that was both affordable and gave solid results without crazy irritation. I didnt see the point in paying $80 for a retinol when it usually causes me to peel. (I know peeling is normal with retinol, but not if it doesnt improve. mine wouldnt with, i think, 1% products). I saw how quickly this has been selling out and have been in love with simple skin care lately, and I am very impressed already! This stuff is perfect for my skin so far because it easily absorbs and doesnt irritate my sensitive skin! it’s a little sticky at first, but it quickly disappears, especially after moisturizing. You definitely want to put this under your moisturizer tho as if you layer it on top it likely wouldn’t sink into your skin as well with a thicker product underneath. I still think a good moisturizer is important when using any retinol though, especially if you’re new to it, which is why I suggest using this as a serum prior to moisturizing. Prolonged use can cause irritation and break outs if you’re not supplementing with enough moisture to compensate for the retinol!

review_text: The Inkey List Retinol Anti-Aging Serum was my first experience with a Retinol product and I didn’t know what to expect. At first I was afraid to use it, but once I did I was surprised at how gentle and non-irritating it was. It has a light, creamy, gel-like texture that is kind of yellow in color. It has a very mild scent that reminds me of lanolin. I washed and dried my face before applying a pea-sized amount to my face and neck. It absorbed right into my skin and felt hydrating, but as the instructions say, you need to apply moisturizer over it, so I applied my night cream over it. The first 2 nights it made my skin feel warm, but in a nice way, for about 5 minutes. After 2 days of use that sensation was gone. This product has made my skin feel extra soft and helped reduce the look of fine lines. I have mild rosacea and it actually seems to calm some of the redness for me. It takes it’s sweet time though so you need to be patient. I have been using nightly for a month now and will continue to do so as part of my nightly routine. The Inkey List product line is so affordable, I will definitely be buying more of their products to use. I highly recommend this for an affordable option to try a gentle retinol.

review_text: Regretfully, sometimes no matter how much you read and research, you make a mistake purchase. I am just glad this wasn’t a costly one & is still perfectly fine for use in other ways. The mica is literally why I originally steered clear of eye creams like the tiny FAB niacinamide one as it’s SO obvious in that one it looks like makeup rather than skincare. But the blurring technology in this one is also just a cosmetic feature rather than an active solution, be it short term or long term, it’s not doing your skin any help, just masking the issue.That being said, I decided the metal applicator tip feels nice, the product feels lovely on the skin, I will just use this as a face serum and massage for when I wake up. Other ingredients in this are great - ginseng, centella asiatica, jojoba, rice bran derivatives, and some other notable ingredients you’ll find in a good standard cream that is significantly more expensive than this. review_text: This is my very first Sephora review, after being an active shopper for 5+ years -- so that shows you that I have f.e.e.l.i.n.g.s about this product. I’ve used a handful of Inkey list products (Q10, Retinol, Polyglutamic) and have appreciated each one for being effective while also very cost effective and I love that all of their products are clean. But this eye cream mangled my eyes. I purchased this about 1.5 months ago, used it for 4 days -- over which time the product went from feeling nice upon application (the metal applicator tip has a nice cooling effect), to stinging a little (I had also been in the sun more than normal so I dismissed it the first time it happened) to stinging so bad I had to immediately wash it off. But worst of all, my woes didn’t end on day 4. Since then for the last month. Again, MONTH of not using this product my whole orbital area has been so dry and sensitive that most anything (including other products I’ve used for years) stings and I wake up to dry, peely, scaly patches above and below my eye -- something, I as a summer “normal“ and winter “dry“ skin person has NEVER experienced before in my life. So now my eye area looks worse (and also god awfully wrinkled) than it ever has -- still after a month of only using the most hydrating products (no actives whatsoever) and having to apply something 3 times a day just to keep the scales at bay. Honestly, if I could go back knowing what I do I would have happily bought a $100 eye cream that isn’t going to ruin my skin. HUGE MISS FOR THE INKEY LIST. This will be returned the first chance after stores reopen.

review_text: These work wonders for dark circles that are hereditary. Over time, they are lessened. What I do is wear them overnight (yes, they stay on thru the night) and remove in the morning. When I take them off, I look at them and if there is still product on them, I put them back in the tray (on the strips that protect the adhesive) and will use them again and again until the product has been completely used. I am able to use each set of patches anywhere between 3 and 6 times. I have tried them on “tired eyes” when my circles are prominent solely due to lack of sleep but I don’t get the same results. I think these are best for hereditary circles. They lighten them enough where it takes several years off my age (I’m nearly 40 and have been considering tear trough filler as a gift to myself to help with my circles which have been prominent since I was about 16). To see if they would work well for you, go in a room with good lighting and see if different angles make your circles disappear, if your circles are only visible in certain angles, these will help you. You will notice a difference after each use, but continued use will help lessen them each time. In my experience, the results seem to be lasting... but if they get worse due to lack of sleep, once I’ve caught up on sleep, they seem to need more work again. These patches used overnight and then followed up in the morning with an under eye brightener or concealer meant to use color correction for days circles tend to make hereditary circles vanish or barely visible. I don’t wear much makeup at all (my all over face “makeup” is just Dr Jart color correcting treatment (I have rosacea so it corrects my redness), no foundation, and I like the Becca under eye brightening corrector (but since that won’t be an option soon, I really like the Charlotte Tilbury magic vanish... the CT texture is amazing and works so well and is a great replacement). Between the patches and an under eye color corrector, my circles are barely seen.

review_text: I didn’t expect much from these, to be honest. I’m a big fan of traditional hydrocolloid blemish stickers, but those are not very effective on under-the-skin zits. Well, I get one specific hormonal, under-the-skin zit on my chin each and every month around my period. It happened to be on my face while I was in Sephora picking something else up, so I decided to give these a shot and used it for the first time last night. I really wasn’t expecting much because they seemed gimmicky and the only acne fighting ingredient in it is niacinamide, which hasn’t done much for me in the past. The application was simple; I applied my normal skincare, gave it about 15 minutes to soak in, then wiped the area clean so the sticker would adhere. You definitely feel the tips going in, but it’s not painful and it doesn’t hurt once applied. I left it on overnight. In the morning, it was still adhered, the tips had dissolved, and my zit was much smaller, though not completely gone. This puts this product in the “special occasion“ category for me. At $3 a patch, it’s not worth it for me to use regularly. But I can see myself using them once a month when my regular pimple first shows up to minimize it and then let it heal naturally, or using them if I have something coming up where I want my skin to look really good and need a blind pimple gone fast. Overall, it works, but it’s too expensive for regular use.

review_text: I am the lucky sufferer of a variety of kinds of acne at 36 years old, so I was able to try these on a couple of different types of blemish. They worked on some, helped on others with downsides, and didn’t work at all on some. The first patch I used, I used on a tight, small, itchy blemish between my eyebrows. I applied the patch as part of evening skincare. Application is relatively simple, although I don’t find it as adhesivey as I’d like, but YMMV. You can actually feel the like micro needles penetrating your skin-- it actually feels like needles!-- which I didn’t expect and thought was really cool. When I woke up and peeled it off, the contents of the blemish came out super easily and... that was that. By the end of the day that day, it was healed and it didn’t scar. But I also tried it on another identical blemish a week or two later, and it didn’t do bupkis. Nothing. So. This was the case, to varying degrees, with two or three of these patches. I also tried this patch on a softer blemish on a softer part of my face: the end of my nose. It’a very unusual spot for a blemish for me, so having already had great luck previously mentioned, I was STOKED to get it addressed immediately. I slept with a patch on it, and in the morning I was able to easily extract the blemish... but it didn’t heal. For DAYS. Weeks later I still have a bit of discoloration, and I put absolutely zero pressure on it. So. I love the concept here but I’m afraid it just didn’t quite work for me and my skin. They’re also expensive enough for me to be hesitant to give them another try.

So will be reviewing each that I’ve tried-Line and wrinkle- I used these on some fine lines on my forehead, 2 patches one night and 2 patches the next night. But, after using these you couldn’t see any lines and my makeup was smooth. It only lasted a couple of days though- my lines are now back. The needles do stain your under eyes yellow, don’t be alarmed like I was though- it washes off easily with water. Blemish- these didn’t work for me at all. I tried using them on some hormonal acne, nothing major, and the next morning there was no difference. Was disappointed with these.Overall I thought these were ok, hence the 3 stars. I love Dr.Jart+ products, but the only patch I was wow’ed by was the under eye patch. For $18, would recommend trying them and seeing if it works for you, but I will only continually purchase the under eye ones.

I would be very very careful with this eye cream and if puffy balls of fluid start accumulating under your eyes while using it, please know it is this eye cream and very likely not something else.

review_text: I loved the idea of a vitamin C sunscreen, but this leaves a lot to be desired. I have sensitive combo skin prone to hyperpigmentation with increasing winter dryness. I used 2 pumps to cover my cheeks, where I have the most sun damage, and applied another sunblock over the whole face, and on days I have meetings, some makeup over that.I used it for over a month, and didn’t notice any lasting difference in my skin. It did look a little glossy when I applied it on my face in the mornings and it didn’t irritate my sensitive skin, so I feel neutral about it. The occasional day I skipped this, I didn’t miss it or feel like my face was dry or anything. It didn’t seem to interfere with any makeup application (liquid foundation, a bit of powder on places that need it) for me. TEXTURE was weird, and at first, it was mostly a runny yellowish oil with some foamy/creamy looking streaks, and now it’s mostly the creamy looking stuff and just a little oil. I shook the bottle before every application, and it never looked like the product photos. PACKAGING HAS MAJOR ISSUES. I generally like pump bottles, but this is crap and a waste of plastic to create a fat ball around an internal container of 1 oz. of product. The little plastic pump button gets stuck every time so I have to pull it up with my fingers before I can squeeze out another pump of product. Also, there’s obviously a fair amount of product left but the pump sputters and doesn’t pull out much product now, so instead of 2 pumps, I’m pumping 5-10 times, each time spitting out little spattery bits. The 1 oz. bottle lasted about 6 weeks of near daily use of 2 pumps of product, the last week dispensing 1 pump’s worth after repeated tries until I got frustrated and moved on. I have lots of 1 oz. bottles of different serums. I know what 1 oz. looks like and how long it should last. This container is making lots of waste of product and plastic. For $46, I wish the product looked like the photos and had a better pump.

review_text: Daily Dose Vitamin C + SPF as the name suggests, is a combination of sunscreen and Vitamin C brightening complex which consist of Vitamin C, Niacinamide, and Kakadu Plum Extract. As we all know, Vitamin C is only efficient when worn with sunscreen but if you are like me, you probably left your home countless times without applying sunscreen first. This ingenious product not only protects the skin from further sun damage but brightens at the same time. Daily Dose comes packaged in an adorable plastic bottle with a tiny pump which makes dispensing the product a breeze. The lightweight and slightly oily serum spreads easily, thanks to its thin consistency, and is absorbed within a few seconds. At first, your skin might look a little bit greasy but don’t worry, once the serum is completely absorbed you will be left with luminous skin. Unlike a lot of other sunscreen, Daily Dose does not leave a white case on the face. At first, I was worried about the effectiveness (sun protection) due to its almost liquid consistency but it held up well in Florida (88 degree, sunny & humid) weather. Even though the product can be worn by itself, it is recommended to use a facial sunscreen on top of Daily Dose for extra sun protection. [Gifted by Supergoop in exchange for my honest opinion]

review_text: i received this product from supergoop for free to test out. i was really curious about this product and i have heard a lot of people talking about it. the product application is really nice and it leaves a glowy finish. but unfortunately the benefits stop there for me. i have used it mostly as the serum step in my skincare and it didn’t pill or interact badly with anything else. however, where this product confuses me is it’s actual ability to function as both a good vitamin c serum and a sunscreen. if applied as the serum step in a skincare routine the skincare going on after will most likely break up the protective film sunscreen leaves on the skin and will lessen the protection. and if applied as the final step in a skincare routine the vitamin c will not be able to really absorb through a moisturizer and steps prior and the benefits will probably be minimal. this product is unique and innovative but where it concerns me is it’s ability to provide enough sun protection if used as the only form of sunscreen in a skincare routine. i used another sunscreen while using this to make sure that there was enough protection. i also finished using this product in less than a month because it is fairly small. i’d say that if you’re thinking of trying this to purchase with the mindset of it being a decent vitamin c serum and that you would probably want to use another sunscreen in your routine.

review_text: There are two way to look at this very unique product from Supergoop:1) A vitamin C serum with the added bonus of SPF2) An SPF with the added bonus of vitamin CI was lucky enough to be able to get a free bottle of this to try for a few weeks and I tried it both ways over that time. First I treated it like a typical vitamin C serum - just used a couple pumps under my usual moisturizer and followed it with my regular sunscreen. The serum has a lovely milky texture that is very moisturizing. If you’re someone with dry skin that has been having trouble finding a moisturizing vitamin C, I think this could be a great fit with the bonus of extra SPF to keep the vitamin C fresh. Secondly, I tried it as a regular SPF after my regular routine, about 4-5 pumps to get the full SPF 40. I found this to be a little too dewy even for my dry skin BUT it does give your skin a lovely plumped up look which I found to be helpful on days I was using a more mattifying makeup products over it or going for a more glowly look. Makeup did not pill over this.I think this Vitamin C/SPF hybrid is going to be a great fit for people that are simply looking for a vitamin C (particularly normal to dry skin folks) and will get the benefit of a little extra SPF layering. Or, normal to combination skin folks who are looking for a REALLY simplified morning routine. I think this would make a good “one-and-done“ product for those that just like to splash their face with water and put one product on in the morning. It certainly has enough moisture for those with more balanced or combination skin types that like a dewy finish to use on its own.For me personally, I’m pretty happy with my current Vitamin C and SPF products. But I’m still happy to have this in my SPF lineup to use as a vitamin C during drier winter month, a serum-y reapplication sunscreen, or to prep my skin for certain makeup looks.

review_text: I love Supergoop and have converted to become a daily SPF user thanks to their PLAY Everyday lotion, PLAY Body Mousse, and Superscreen. So when I heard about this newest addition from them that includes Vitamin C, I was very excited to try this out! I did receive this product free of charge from Supergoop for my honest review. The consistency is thin and fluid, so application was easy and it blended in effortlessly without leaving a white cast. I used this after cleansing, softener, and a different serum (without vitamin C). There was no scent but the “sunscreen smell“ is definitely more pronounced in this serum than in all the other Supergoop products I’ve used. I’d also say the glow this product leaves is also more pronounced, so even for someone like me who loves glow, it was a bit too much, bordering on greasiness. Once applied, my dry skin still felt like it required a moisturizer on top. While Superscreen would have done the job as my final moisturizer during warm summer months, going without a heavy moisturizing cream as I normally do during winter was just not an option. However, it felt counterintuitive putting a heavy moisturizer on top of this serum which already had sunscreen in it. So I struggled with where it would fit into my routine, especially during winter. While I wanted to love this product for its duality, I could only see it fitting into a morning routine during warm summer weather or for someone who doesn’t have dry skin needing extra moisture. I will forever be a Supergoop fan, but more likely to use another vitamin C serum without spf and then layering Supergoop’s other great sunscreens as my final layer over heavy moisturizer.

review_text: Ok first of all, I’m shocked that this combination of ingredients has not been created by anyone (as far as I know) up until now.  Like I never knew that Vitamin C wasn’t really effective without sunscreen, so this combo of two of the biggest anti-aging fighters is genius.  Another thing that I learned is that not all Vitamin C’s are the same so I appreciate that this is a potent version and stable with the sunscreen. The actual product is one of the glowiest hydrators I have ever used and is my new favorite step of my morning routine.  I’m all about a super glowy, natural complexion so this is everything for me.  The second I apply, it feels like my skin is drinking up a big glass of water.  I do have combo skin and am definitely oily in the T zone so I can see how some people might find this too shiny for them, but I appreciate how hydrating it is and just a little finishing powder in the T zone and I’m good to go.  I have been using this for almost 3 weeks and am starting to see some of my acne marks fade along with brightened skin.  Because it’s so hydrating it has replaced my hyaluronic acid and other serums in the AM, so I just use them at night now.  I use 2 pumps of Daily Dose after cleansing and toning, then mix a couple drops of Drunk Elephant D-Bronzi (another obsession for its natural glowiness and antioxidant ingredients) with Superscreen and/or Glowscreen depending on my mood and I’m set for the day! Planning on using this forever.  I am interested to see how long it lasts using 2 pumps per day because it’s a little pricey. But it seems like a little goes a long way as long as you layer with other SPF and as Nam Vo (the glow queen) always says “it ain’t cheap, but neither are you“ lol <3

review_text: For reference, my skin: fair, combo/oily, adult acne, some rosaceaI received a sample of this in a gift bag, so really had no expectations for it, but turns out I absolutely love it. It’s very watery, more of a toner than a lotion - I use it nightly under any serums (usually vitamin C or a retinol) and a night cream. It provides the perfect boost of moisture if your skin is naturally dry or simply irritated. I found it help calm my summer blotchiness/rosacea without breaking me out at all. It also seems to cut the burn/irritation of any harsher products applied on top. I’d say it’s slightly less hydrating than a pure hyaluronic acid serum, but much more calming, which is exactly what my skin type needs. It lasts quite a while, too. I put maybe a dime size squirt in my palms and rub it on my face that way and, with once daily use, the sample bottle I’ve had for months isn’t even halfway gone. Overall, if you want a gentle serum/toner to use under (or after) harsher products, or if you just need a boost of calming moisture, I’d highly recommend trying this. Just for comparison, I’d say the closest thing to this I’ve tried has been Glow Recipe’s Avocado Ceramide Serum (different ingredients, but same claims of redness relief and moisture) and I found this one more moisturizing and MUCH more calming (and more wallet-friendly!).

review_text: I follow a 4-5 step Korean skin care system that involves me using different products (Asian and American) in layering the products to achieve my skin goals (hydrated and healthy), AM and PM. My skin care process usually involves layering multiple toners (Korean) to get the hydration I need, so this product being similar to a treatment lotion, it was simple to follow directions and use. This lotion gives an earthy, mushroom, patchouli scent, which I felt like was unnecessary given the pretty decent ingredients list. It was just surprising to see that mushroom was a little bit further down on the ingredients list, but I was more surprised at the other great ingredients listed on the product packaging. As an essence or treatment lotion, it does provide that initial step of hydration and possible soothing of the skin. However, I don’t think it packs enough of a punch (in terms of hydration) to be used on its own before moisturizer if you have oily skin and don’t use cream moisturizers (I.e. gel). It would need to be layered with yet another item, another toner or another serum, before moisturizer. It’s a viscous treatment lotion that is easy to pat into the skin for quick absorption. It’s not tacky or sticky. The scent might require some getting used to but it’s okay, but for some people who may be more sensitive to scents, that may be an issue. I feel like this treatment lotion would be great for someone who hasn’t incorporated any treatment lotions, essences or serums in their skin care routine and are looking for an additional boost to increase their skin hydration and improve their skin barrier. I will use up all that I have but I will not be purchasing this product again because I feel like there are other options available to to me that may do the same job, if not more, but would cost less.

review_text: I’ve never heard of a lotion that applies like a toner so I have nothing to compare this to, but I’ve been pleased overall. The packaging is pretty yet simple, and the smell is very light but pleasant. I don’t remember reading on the packaging that there was hyaluronic acid, but reading it online makes it even more of a plus for me! I have semi-sensitive skin and have a tendency to get red with the slightest bit of irritation, but this lotion hasn’t broken me out or irritated my skin at all. I will say, I wish the directions/description was a little better on the box and on the bottle. I’m a little perplexed as for when to use this in my skincare routine. Before toner? After toner? I enjoy how lightweight this product is, as I can’t stand feeling like there’s 8 layers of products on my face. If I had to make any complaint, it would be that the product feels mildly oily on my skin after applying, but that seems to go away within a few minutes. I’m curious to see longer term results, as I know mushrooms have some great health benefits! I have combination to oily skin, especially in my T-Zone but I’m not sure I would recommend this to someone with dryer skin unless they were to use this product in addition to a heavier cream moisturizer.

review_text: Y’all….I’m begging for everyone to read instructions. When you initially take this out of the package it will have a yellow tube in the middle of the brush holding in the powder. You need to take a pair of tweezers or something to pull it out. Once you pull it out the powder is now loose and you can twist the bottom, holding the brush upside down, and powder will fill the brush. I usually use this for touch ups in the summer. It is definitely not full coverage, just something to slip in the bag and take out for a nice touch of extra SPF. It’s not a powder foundation, nor will it super set your makeup. This is purely for touch ups after applying a good spf before makeup. I personally love it, it’s not messy and the cap holds on in my bag. It’s small enough to take to theme parks in the summer, or out by the beach. If you simply use it for touch ups it will last a very long time, if you are looking for an everyday, heavy duty powder - look for bare minerals or something that has SPF in it with bigger packaging/more coverage.

I absolutely adored the idea of this product, and was hoping it would become a summer staple for me. review_text_clean: I was so thankful when this came in the mail on Saturday, I had a morning photoshoot in direct sunlight and expected to start sweating and have to powder. I started with the Sheerscreen sunscreen primer by Supergoop as the last step in my skincare routine, as my sunscreen base. (I will review that on its own page!)I’ve been using this every 2 hours through the day as an alternative to my usual touch up face powder, and it’s great! The twist- lock is genius- I get just the amount of powder I need, gently contour it in with the attached brush, then lock the twist lock to seal the powder in, pop up the small brush barrier, and put the lid back on, and it’s purse safe, no powder spillage. The brush barrier is also a brilliant detail- it’s a small plastic tube that pulls up towards the tip of the brush, before you put the lid on, to keep the bristles straight and prevent the lid from bending them.Very fast and easy to use and put away, they really thought of everything.

The translucent shade is great!

review_text: Writing a non-“incentivized“ review as someone who paid for this product to try with their own money (rare these days). I use this product together with their Slushy serum+moisturizer (which is one of my all time favorite skincare products fyi). I was super excited to try this serum since I am a huge fan of the other one. I found this product is just ok. In my opinion it doesn’t really add anything to my routine, I haven’t noticed any changes in my skin either positive or negative. I can live without it and simplify my life. One thing I don’t like about it is the smell. It’s “superfood“ and it smells like superfoods. It smells like I’m smearing kale and grass on my face... not the worst thing I guess (I actually love kale), but its not the nicest either. Texture and color isn’t as appealing as other serums. Its always fun to try new products but I’d rather save the money next time and buy more Slushy instead. One big positive about this product is that there is so much product in the bottle, which is very nice for the price. It lasts much much longer than the Slushy. I’m just trying to use this bottle up and I feel like I can’t, I have had it for probably 6 months now. Slushy in comparison only lasts me only a month and a half with twice daily use. I wish I could have tried a sample before purchasing the full size. While I’m not crazy about this Green Machine serum I am loving the Green Machine face mask and Slushy serum. I love this brand and many of their products this one was just a miss for me. I wanted to write a real review because when people get the item for free or get paid to write a review they tend to overhype it or are less critical than if they paid full price, and tbh I think thats exactly what happens with most of these reviews.

I think most of my acne and pigmentation issues are resolved from those products, however this is a nice gentle formula to use during the day that helps my skin feel replenished. If you want to add Vitamin C to your routine THIS IS THE BEST VITAMIN C you can pick.

review_text: As much as I love to purchase skincare and pretend like I have a stringent 10-step routine, I just can’t keep it up. In all honesty, I’m really low-maintenance when it comes to skincare and wind up slapping a few products on my face both at night and in the morning instead of making it some big ritual. While most derms would tell you it’s great to stick to the basics, my skin really doesn’t “glow” without some extra effort. Enter Green Machine, which I’ve been testing out now for about two weeks. I was immediately interested in trying this after reading it mixes some of my favorite standalone ingredients - namely fatty acids and vitamin c. When I got it in, I immediately noticed there’s no fragrance. Win! It has a lovely jelly/bouncy texture that I’ve found is really easy to slap on my face, neck, and chest without getting tacky or pilling up under any sunscreen or Foundation. I’m weird about texture, but this product gets high marks from me on being so easy. Over the past few weeks, I’ve noticed subtle changes in my skin tone and texture. I have fair skin and suffer from dark spots after acne has healed up, and I found this did a really great job of lightening those. I also have larger pores on my nose and across my upper cheeks, and this product has helped tighten those a bit (which has kept me from going ham picking at them!). I’m sure with longer use I will see more improvements, but I’m here to tell you that you should try this out for yourself. This is truly the best product for low-maintenance folks as it gives you the benefit of many different skin-repairing ingredients in a ready-made formula that doesn’t leave you worried you put something on in the wrong order. Bonus points for the cute packaging - the colors remind me of summer!

review_text: Dermalogica recently launched a new hydration serum, the Circular Hydration Serum, and I had a chance to test it free in exchange for my honest review. The Circular Hydration Serum has 3 goals: to immediately quench dehydrated skin, to replenish skin from within and to prevent future dehydration. The ingredients highlighted to achieve the goals are: an enhanced form of Hyaluronic Acid, an Algae-infused moisturizing matrix and Polyglutamic Acid from fermented soy. The serum can be used morning & night.The Circular Hydration Serum is very silky, and slightly viscous in texture. It’s very good, my skin feels quenched and hydrated, but the feeling doesn’t last near as long as promised. My skin is dry, during the shifting weather here in Ottawa, often dehydrated as well. My occasional sensitivity reacted at first, with a hint of irritation, then settled after further use.  It’s possible I had to get used to the oils in the serum.Overall, while effective, the Circular Hydration Serum doesn’t feel like the right hydrating serum for me. Perhaps a person with another skin type would get better results.#giftedbydermalogica

A postbiotic blend of Lactobacillus Ferment and Avena Extract helps to balance skin’s microbiome.”performance | full star | wowowowow! This serum truly does all that! review_text: This product was used on my skin when I had a facial at Pro Sports Club in Bellvue, Washington. I asked what she was using and she told me. I purchased a bottle from them along with a Booster Detox. I was told how to use the Lotus oil and the Detox. I was concerned about the oily appearance of the Lotus oil, but after I gave it a try, it is amazing. My acne prone skin is getting better and it is not as oily in the T-Zone area. Yes, I still have adult acne at the age of 63. Have been dealing with dermatologists for years without any long term results.. My skin is soft and supple now. I still use my moisturizer on top of the application of lotus oil. I wait about five minutes or so before applying the moisturizer. I was told to use the Booster Detox only once a week with the oil. I have not used the Booster Detox yet, and my skin is still responding to the Lotus oil. Great Product, and I have tried everything. This works well on my acne prone skin!! Keep it away from your eye area; it is not for the eyes. I was also told to only use two ( 2 ) drops and do not rub it in; pat it on the skin instead. That is enough.. You will have a tendency to want to use more and rub, but the 2 drops is enough and pat in on... It’s there and working.

I just apply the oil at least 15 minutes before I apply my makeup so it can absorb! If you have oily or acne prone skin try this, you won’t regret it!! I’m using it everyday as a preventive, and if I do get a cyst I’ll apply a tad extra on the cyst itself. I love this oil, I’m a believer in oils now! review_text: First, let me say that it’s take a LONG time to learn that if you’re not born with flawless skin, then when it comes to taking care of it, LESS is MORE. I totally believe in using minimal products to balance the skin rather than trying every new exfoliating serum, brush, mask, you name it - I’ve tried it all and have done too much.I got back into using facial oils about 5 years ago, kind of off an on, before every major cosmetics brand was pushing their products. First used Dr. Hauschka’s Normalizing Day Oil, then forgot about it - obviously it didn’t change my life. Then went really far out there and used natural Emu oil on my skin. I had read that it was especially healing for scars, and I wanted to see if it could minimize some light acne scarring I had gotten in my early 20’s. I’m not 31, for the record.More recently, I’ve used the Josie Maran Argan Oil, it was good, but didn’t notice immediate results. Then got the Boscia Tsubaki Oil, which I did really like.About two months ago I was cornered by a Clarins rep in a Sephora in West Palm Beach, FL, and she really convinced me to try their stuff. I left with a new moisturizer, and facial serum in addition to a generous sample of the Lotus Oil.This is the best yet.I will add now that I only exfoliate, gently, once a week - even though I want to do more to try to get rid of some congested spots, or clogged pores on my nose - and this oil has really done wonderful things when it comes to balancing out my skin’s oil production.I used to have many bumps, built-up sebum, that have just started to melt away after using this nightly. I was instructed to use this only at night, and not add anything to it. I’ve done so religiously and after about 5 weeks don’t use any makeup to blend my skin tone or cover redness.I highly recommend getting this OR getting a little sample, it’ll last forever!

review_text: I really, really, really love this cream. I feel like I’m pampering myself when I use Absolue, and that means I start my day feeling good both inside and out.  Marvelous product; I recommend to anyone who wants a moisturizer that makes your skin soft as silk.  Definitely going to be a part of my beauty regimen going forward.

review_text: Love this serum. I have tried many vitamin c serums but none of them checked all the boxes. A lot of the vitamin c serums on the market are either too sticky, too oily, or in moisturizer form. Tarte youth or dare are none of those. It absorbed into my skin quickly, didn’t leave a sticky/oily residue, worked perfectly under SPF and makeup, and most importantly, made a difference in my skin. I had purchased it to help lighten some post inflammation hyperpigmentation (aka some big cystic zit scarring) and was pleasantly surprised by how quickly they lightened after I started using this serum. The other parts of my face are also noticably smoother and even.The main gripe I have with the product is that tarte has decided to tint the serum an orange color so people won’t notice when it has gone off. L ascorbic acid is the most proven effective form of vitamin c (which is part of why I like this serum), but is also known to be unstable and will expire quickly. I’d rather be able to tell when the serum is starting to go off so I can use it up sooner. I also like that the packaging is in pump form to limit air exposure and that it is opaque to limit light exposure. I just wish there was a way to tell how much product is left in the bottle.

review_text: Since I’d never tried anything from Paula’s Choice before I was very happy to be able to be gifted by Paula’s Choice the 25% AHA + 2% BHA peel complimentary to try because it was actually a product that I’d considered purchasing anyway.  I don’t have any “major“ skin issues but as I get a little older I AM noticing more little fine lines and my skin generally isn’t as smooth as I would like it to be so I was hoping that using this solution would improve the overall texture of my skin.  Unfortunately I’m a little disappointed because I really can’t see any noticeable results that this gives me.  Granted, I tend to have somewhat resilient--and not at all sensitive--skin and while this may work better for someone who needs a gentle approach to acids, this may not be quite enough for a more adventurous user.  That’s not to say that it’s a bad product; it just wasn’t a good fit for me.  On the plus side, I haven’t seen any actual negative effects from it but I really haven’t seen any positive ones, either.

review_text: Warning: this product contains glycolic acid, lactic acid, citric acid, and RETINOL!! I bought this product specifically because my skin was in need of extra hydration after regular use of exfoliating acids (in other DDG skincare products). I *thought* this product would be good for my skin since it markets itself as a lightweight drink of water for your skin, I was wrong. It did not increase hydration in my skin (although it is very lightweight and absorbs quickly). If anything, it made my skin barrier more compromised and irritated since applying this product to my skin meant I was applying MORE exfoliating acids to my already exfoliated skin. The ingredients in this product are noncomedogenic, but if you have sensitive/dry/dehydrated skin AND you’re already using exfoliating acids in other skincare products, this probably isn’t the best product for you. I totally think this can be a great product for someone with oily skin, someone living in hot/humid weather, or for someone who is NOT already using exfoliating acids in their other skincare products. Otherwise, stay clear of this product. I have had better hydration results using Kiehl’s Hydro-Plumping Re-Texturizing Serum Concentrate (fav!), Drunk Elephant’s B-Hydra Intensive Hydration Serum, or Tatcha’s Gold Camellia Beauty Oil.

review_text: I got this as part of a package bonus with the purchase of Dr. Gross’ facial steamer and I instantly fell in love! I used it one day only and felt like I could go without foundation as it left such a beautiful, dewy look. My husband even thought I was getting more rest and work wasn’t stressful because I looked so refreshed after a week of using the booster! Throughout winter I never had any facial driness issues unlike the past when I wasn’t using the Clinical Hydration Booster. To remove any doubt of its effectiveness, my young toddler ended up needing to be hospitalized for a couple weeks in the middle of the coldest part of our winter in the north east. We had to protect her from any outside germs that could cause illness which meant CONSTANT hand washing and sanitizer use which wrecked the skin on my hands. The top of my hands started to get tiny cracks, the skin which is usually soft and supple turned rough and dull, and I used every intensive moisturizer out there and nothing seemed to work (even another hyaluronic acid serum Sephora sells that YouTubers rave about). I was putting this hydration booster on my face one morning and decided to put some on my dry hands, and immediately they weren’t itching from dryness anymore. I used this serum only a couple times a day for the next few days and my hands were back to before I had to wash them 30 times a day, even though I was still washing them like crazy at the hospital! My mother, who suffers from dry hands in the winter, tried this hydration booster after I told her what I noticed and after years of cracked winter hands had soft, smooth hands again. Even though this is technically for your face, I always use it on my hands and face now because it works to really keep my skin hydrated and supple. The only downfall is that there is glycerin in the booster which gives skin a slightly tacky feel, but once I put foundation on, I hardly notice.

After just one use my skin is completely smooth, the few bumps I had disappeared, and my skin was so soft, I couldn’t stop touching it, with the back of my hand of course! There is a technique to using all La Mer moisturizers and the little spoon it comes with will help ensure you don’t use too much at once. I also only use as a night cream bc #1) you should be using a moisturizer with SPF in the day time and #2) you will get clogged skin if you use this under the sun!!

review_text: I will never understand why La Mer discontinued their beautiful Gel Cream and replaced it with this flaming hot mess. I’m switching away from the La Mer brand in general right now, because while they were the best thing in skincare 15 years ago, so many wonderful new brands are out on the market that are just as gentle and healing and don’t test on animals. Good riddance, La Mer and parent company Estée Lauder.

review_text: I got this in the trial mini size because I’ve never used a La Mer product, and thought I’d check out the hype. I use SKII Essence and serum, Claudalie toner and mist, and have been trying out Tatcha indigo cream for two months now (and feeling meh about it).I’m 45, with normal to slightly dry skin, roseacea and sun damage. Goes on smooth and a little goes a long way. It does not break me out, and absorbs fast. I noticed a plumper/smoother texture on Day 2, which makes it hard to figure out long term of this will actually improve my skin, but does mean my skin looks amazing.The biggest difference i notice is, usually even wth SFP50 sunscreen on, my face flushes in hot sun, and in the evening is still red when i cleanse - but not using this. I took me three days to figure out, the only difference in my routine was the gelv cream. My roseacea has been kept in check! That, combined with the excellent texture improvement and fast absorption make this 5 stars for me, even at the astronomical price.Silicone for me isn’t inherently “gross“ in cosmetics - it’s also the basis of undereye and decollete patches that prevent wrinkles, and it’s likely why i see results overnight with this gel, because it’s retaining moisture in my skin readout well, and helping calm my roseacea. I can’t use silicone primers, because they DO break me out, and is not consider this equivalent in texture or weight at all to them. I don’t find it to sit on the surface, or be sticky on me. As someone who didn’t try the old version and not dealing with acne (which seems to be a lot of those frustrated with the reformulation), i really love this product, and find it gives me at least short term results better than most products. I plan to buy a jar to see how it performs over 6-12 months.

review_text: Originally when I got my first set, I was quite pleased with the creams and the lactic acid, but as my skin is oily, I did not use the oil. I forgot I even had it. This was my first experience with products containing squalane, and I was pleased to find my skin seemed to love it. I do not love hyaluronic acid; it irritates my skin, and because it is in EVERYTHING these days, I wind up with it in layers of products and I believe this results in foundations separating. I’ve really been having trouble in this regard, so I’m delighted to find a moisturizer that uses squalane instead. Now, recently I got hold of a benzoil peroxide cream that, unlike the usual stuff you get over the counter, was twice the concentrate (which I did not know at the time). After just two applications my face burned, itched, reddened, and finally peeled!  Horrible. Of course I discontinued use and threw it away. But my face needed repair, badly. Good moisturizer helped but not enough. I remembered the Biossance oil in this set, and dug it out of the drawer. It soothed my skin immediately. I applied it twice daily for a little over a week, and it did the trick. My normal (oily) skin finds it too much to use daily, but I apply it after a long bath or other drying environment and it makes my skin hydrated, luminous, and healthy looking.The eye cream in this set is one of my top five favorite products.

review_text: This set is definitely a Biossance “Dream Team“! The lactic acid serum is amazing. I use this nightly and my face is perfectly smooth and fresh in the morning. The omega moisturizer is exactly what my skin needs, especially in dry CO winters. I use this day and night in the winter and just night during the summer. The algae eye cream is exactly what my eyes need. No matter how tired I am (mid-40’s, mother, working, and a student) my eyes and skin feel so much brighter with this line! And the icing on the cake is the rose oil! For a few years I used to put rose oil on first before moisturizer.
